items.headline: Geopolymer stones created by mixing mineral powders rich in silica and alumina with alkaline solutions
items.summary:
- Geopolymer stones created by mixing mineral powders rich in silica and alumina with alkaline solutions
- Geopolymers harden at low temperatures and can be poured into molds while wet
- Stones can be shaped and joined seamlessly before hardening
- Scoop marks found on blocks suggest material removal while stone was still in soft or semi-plastic state
- Similar scoop marks appear at multiple global sites including Aswan Quarry (Egypt), Stonehenge (England), Domus de Janas (Sardinia), and Tlaloc Statues (Mexico)
- Seamless joints and precise polygonal masonry at Inca sites suggest controlled shaping rather than carving
- Absence of visible tool marks on many blocks, particularly chisel scars or percussion marks

items.headline: Land purchased April 16th, 1805 by Marmont from Yan Herson Fonhingo
items.summary:
- Land purchased April 16th, 1805 by Marmont from Yan Herson Fonhingo
- Three soldier guardians stationed: Louis Fe, Jean Baptiste de Larouche, and Barant Phillips
- Officially renamed August 17th, 1806 by King Louis Bonaparte to Pyramid of Austerlitz after Battle of Austerlitz
- Wooden obelisk demolished in 1808 by royal order; stone memorial plaques removed by inhabitants
- 1848 documentation shows step-exterior disappeared, spiral pathway replaced by 1895 with straight staircase
- 1894 renovation by estate owner Johannes Bernardes Dubau; new stone obelisk designed by architect Dave Fond completed October 17th, 1894
- 2001-2004 extensive restoration attempted to recreate original 1804 appearance; damaged by 2003 drought and 2004 rainfall
- October 2007: 1.2 million euros allocated for step design restoration by Utre municipality
- 2010-2012: New pile foundation installed; 160 poles of 4 m and 250 poles of 5 m driven into pyramid to strengthen structure
- 2019: New sod edge constructed on pyramid summit
items.post_text: The Pyramid of Austerlitz has been through A LOT - lost its wooden obelisk in 1808, major restorations in 1894, 2001-04, and 410 foundation poles (160 of 4m + 250 of 5m) in 2010-12 to prevent collapse 🛠️

items.headline: August de Marmont inspired by Giza pyramids during Napoleon's Egypt occupation
items.summary:
- August de Marmont inspired by Giza pyramids during Napoleon's Egypt occupation
- Marmont stationed in Betavian Republic (Netherlands) in 1804 during Third Coalition War
- Monument construction began September 10th, 1804 on Amerz ridge approximately 55 m above NAP (Normal Amsterdam water level)
- Pyramid built from earth and peat with stepped design mimicking original Giza appearance
- Square base measured 43.60 x 43.60 m, top 6 x 6 m, height 36 m
- Construction completed October 7th, 1804 after 27 days using sandbags passed soldier-to-soldier
- Lead tube containing protocol, soldier names, gold-silver coin bearing Napoleon's image, and Legion of Honor medallion sealed at apex
- 40-step stairway constructed with 48 cm high steps; 13 m wooden obelisk added atop pyramid over 5 days
- Construction cost 8,100 guilden (only tools, obelisk, and stone plaques required payment)
